notes: New rule, graded against the current text: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call. It is not in idiomatic-elixir/ at 0397dec (git diff 0397dec adds it to SKILL.md, and changes the Use ETS example in references/processes.md to build table_options before :ets.new/2), so 2026-10-22-b has no verdict for it; it is graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-check-7/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json. The sentence that decides the verdict is "When an argument is a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines, build it first under a name that says what it is, write it one field per line, and set each multi-line statement apart with a blank line." Violating runs: 1 of 5 (sonnet-2); check-7 had 0 of 4, check-6 3 of 4.

Every call whose argument is a map, struct or keyword list spanning several lines, per run. Opus-1 has one, :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 128), named first at lines 120-126 (table_options = [ / :named_table, / :public, / :ordered_set, / read_concurrency: true, / write_concurrency: true / ]), one field per line, with a blank line between it and the call (line 127): the processes.md example with :ordered_set. Sonnet-1 has one, :ets.new(name, table_options) (line 125), named first at lines 117-123 with the same five fields one per line and blank lines before (116) and after (124). Sonnet-2 has one and did not name it: :ets.new(requests_table(name), [ / :named_table, / :public, / :ordered_set, / write_concurrency: true / ]) (lines 102-107), the shape the rule forbids; joined, that call is exactly 98 characters, so mix format would have kept it on one line, but the session wrote it across six lines and mix format keeps a list the author broke, so the argument as written spans several lines inline. Its other table's options are inline on one line (line 99), and its two match specs are named (expired line 116, in_window line 141). Haiku-1 and haiku-2 have no such call: their :ets.new/2 options are one-line literals (haiku-1 line 97 :ets.new(name, [:named_table, :public, :ordered_set]); haiku-2 line 108 :ets.new(@table, [:named_table, :public, :ordered_set, write_concurrency: true])) and their match specs are one-line lists of tuples (haiku-1 lines 110, 120; haiku-2 lines 120, 127), so, to check-7's standard that short one-line literals are clean, both are clean. Not counted, as in check-7: sonnet-1's opts = / Keyword.validate!(opts, [:config_path, name: __MODULE__, sweep_interval: @sweep_interval]) (lines 82-83), where mix format wrapped the statement at = but the list stays on one line; one-line GenServer.start_link/3 calls in every run; opus-1's Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy: :one_for_one, name: MyApp.Supervisor) (line 198) after a children list built under a name (lines 191-196); and the moduledoc child lists, all built under children (haiku-1 lines 15-18, whose one tuple mix format wrapped over lines 16-17 around a single-entry keyword list; haiku-2 lines 13-15; sonnet-1 lines 25-29; sonnet-2 lines 20-24). No nested call with its own options appears inside a literal. The transcripts show the first Write of each session already had its final shape: opus-1 and sonnet-1 named table_options, sonnet-2 wrote the inline six-line list, the Haiku runs wrote one-line options.

The other nine rules have unchanged text since 0397dec (the diff also touches How to use this skill, Update structs, the do: rule, the new directive-order rule, Before you finish and testing.md, none on this case's list; in processes.md only the Use ETS example's code changed, not its prose) and are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json: an if on one boolean condition is clean; a single fallible call handled with a case whose success clause returns the next step's result is clean under the with rule (haiku-2 read_config/1 lines 139-145, as opus-1 in 2026-10-22-b); a two-step with whose body returns a third fallible call is not counted (haiku-1 lines 138-140 returning parse_limits(decoded)); a run with no with and no fallible {:ok, _} | {:error, _} call is not exercised (sonnet-1 load_config!/1 and sonnet-2 load_limits!/1 both raise at boot through Code.eval_file/1), as check-6 and check-7 graded such runs; key, row_key, other and similar local names are not counted under Naming, but a single-letter n for a limit is, as 2026-10-22-b counted it for baseline-opus-1 (%{"default" => n} when is_integer(n)); section-label comments are not counted; a start_link/1 with no :name option and a fixed table name violates the responsive rule, as 2026-10-22-b counted for baseline-opus-1; reading the limits file in init/1 is a missed case check but decides no verdict, because the responsive rule names only HTTP calls and large queries as slow work.

Two standard calls decide verdicts here. Opus-1 uses n for a limit eight times (lines 130, 138, 159, 160, 162, 166, 170, 173), the same shape counted for baseline-opus-1 in 2026-10-22-b, so Naming is violated; it is the only single-letter name in the five runs. Haiku-2's start_link/1 ignores every option but :config_path and registers name: __MODULE__ (line 100) over a fixed table @table __MODULE__.Windows (line 57), and check/1 (line 72) takes no server argument, so a test cannot start a second instance; that breaks the responsive rule's :name sentence (in a scratch run a second start_link/1 could not be tried for that reason). Every other run accepts :name and names its table after it (opus-1 line 47, haiku-1 lines 59-60, sonnet-1 line 83, sonnet-2 line 64; sonnet-2's limits table :"#{name}.Limits" at line 148 is built from the start option, not from user data, as check-7 left it).

Designs. All five keep one ETS row per admitted request in a public ordered_set table owned by a GenServer, and the caller inserts its row, counts with :ets.select_count/2 and deletes its row when over the limit, with a handle_info/2 sweep (opus-1 every 30 s, haiku-1 every minute keeping two windows, haiku-2 every 10 s, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 every 30 s), so Pick the abstraction, Use ETS, Keep each process behind one module and the call/cast and per-key cleanup parts of the responsive rule are clean in all five. Limits live as rows in the same table (opus-1, haiku-1), in :persistent_term (haiku-2, sonnet-1), or in a second, protected table (sonnet-2). Every run reads the limits file inside init/1: opus-1 line 97 (:file.consult/1 at line 144), haiku-1 line 95 (File.read/1 at line 138), haiku-2 line 105 (:file.consult/1 at line 140), sonnet-1 line 114 (Code.eval_file/1 at line 157), sonnet-2 line 97 (Code.eval_file/1 at line 126). Only opus-1 compiles its start-up and caller examples as modules (MyApp.Application, a plug, a controller and an Oban worker); sonnet-2 compiles an example MyApp.ReportWorker; the others show callers in the moduledoc.

Verification, in scratch copies under grading9/rate-limiter-skill. All five pass mix format --check-formatted, have no line over 98 characters, and every session ran mix format itself. Haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors. Opus-1's full file fails at import Plug.Conn (line 223) because its example plug, controller and Oban worker need Plug, Phoenix and Oban; lines 1-200 (the limiter and MyApp.Application) compile alone with --warnings-as-errors. In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42, configured at 5; where :name is accepted (all but haiku-2) a second instance under name: :other kept its own count (2 of 50); an injected expired row was removed by one :sweep message and the other rows kept. Haiku-1 compares user IDs through to_string/1 (line 116), so 42 and "42" share a count, as its moduledoc says; the others key by the raw ID. Sonnet-2 takes the default limit from the :default_limit start option (line 95), not from the file, and its moduledoc says the :limits_path fallback uses Application.get_env while configured_limits_path/0 (line 123) calls Application.fetch_env!. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 evaluate their limits files as Elixir code with Code.eval_file/1, documented in the moduledoc.

All five runs have rc 0 and a model_id matching their tier, and their skill_hash, 03a6bb2b11d4ddb04dbddb0f8fcfb5b3ac5c366c89b6b87d05d7f06691a962e3, equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/ (head 3e3581d, uncommitted false).
